GCLI-121 PLAN (the predecessor's, sent to the leader and accepted by (a70)). MEASURED behaviour on dev 3b9662d with a scratch script (analyzePythonCalls on app.py plus m.py, printing bins and callee names): unquoted `x: C` resolves x.meth() to C.meth in every shape (same module, imported, imported under `if TYPE_CHECKING:`, Optional[C], C | None), so the TYPE_CHECKING half is already satisfied unquoted; every QUOTED form is receiverNeedsInference 1 with no edge: x: "C" (same module, a forward reference to a later class, imported, TYPE_CHECKING-imported), x: "m.C", Optional["C"], "C | None", and a quoted TYPE_CHECKING import with an else-branch rebind. Cause: describeAnnotation (src/python/calls.ts ~765) has no string case, so a string annotation is kind other. FIX: add a string case that accepts only a plain, unprefixed, non-concatenated, non-triple-quoted string with no escapes whose text is a name or dotted name, X | None, None | X, Optional[X] or Union[X, None]; it returns the same AnnotationDesc the unquoted form gives, so resolveAnnotationClass is unchanged. calls.ts has no parser handle there, so a small hand-written reader of identifiers, dots, | and brackets does the parsing; anything else is other (f-string, bytes, r-prefix, concatenation, a call, list[C], more than one class, an unterminated string). Strings nested inside Optional[...] or Union[...] go through the same case because the existing subscript code calls describeAnnotation on its arguments. Per (a70) the quoted text is looked up in the scope the unquoted twin uses but with LATER bindings visible (resolveAnnotationClass calls resolveBareName(desc.name, scope, 0) with no use position, which already sees later module bindings; confirm for a function scope), and a name with more than one binding there, or one bound conditionally, refuses.

STANDING RULES AND LESSONS: dispatch-floor.mjs glyph-cli <task> runs before every brief and again with --pr N before review (the leader runs it); the five-pin delta and EVERY created or removed in-repo edge go to the leader BEFORE any clear request; every fixture delta is MEASURED against dev by running both (never state one unmeasured: the predecessor's 'same as dev' on a classmethod fixture was wrong and opum-doc ruled the case conformance to (a13) N8); observed-red mutants and fixtures red on the base and green after are required; one Opus round 1 on each build, a fix push, a second full round if needed, DEC-161 two-round cap (a second block goes to opum-doc); merge with gh pr merge N --squash --match-head-commit <sha> --delete-branch bare and only on the leader's head-pinned clear; never amend or force-push; a conflicted PR is fixed by restoring the conflicting record to its merge-base content in a NEW commit (git show <base>:path > path), never a merge-from-dev (that makes the re-review scope full); run git push and git checkout -b each alone in their own Bash call (a composed push is refused by a hook); never use shell variables or a trailing $/ in write paths or sed expressions that write files (the ownership guard refuses them; use python for in-place edits); a PR body goes in a file via --body-file; format with bunx biome format --write src test (NOT prettier, which reformats whole files); every Quest write needs --actor glyph-cli --actor-kind delegated-agent --accountable-human jdnewhouse; the gated ref is dev, every change lands through a PR; bun test takes about 95 s; export PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v24.22.2/bin:$PATH; tests live in test/python-hops.test.ts (probe/both helpers; append a describe block per task). A PR that is cleared is pinned to one head: do not push to it after the clear without telling the leader the new head.
